commits.message:
Logs that say what the question actually was (#260)

Nobody asked for redaction. It was added on the reasoning that "these logs get
pasted somewhere public during a connector mystery" -- a real risk at *paste*
time, applied as permanent deletion at *write* time, on a single-tenant
service whose only readers are the people who run it.

Two symptoms, both from the same allowlist:

**GitHub was posting to `/webhooks/github` -- plural, not a route -- and every
404 said only that a POST happened.** Not the path with its query, not the
body, not which of GitHub's own headers described the delivery. A week of
"Not Found" answered nothing about what was being asked for.

**An accepted delivery said `pull_request arrived` and nothing else.** Not the
repository, the action, the PR number, or the target branch -- the entire
content of "did the right thing happen". The payload was in Firestore, where
nobody reading a log is looking.

## The inversion

`redact()` was an allowlist: four headers logged, everything else replaced
with `<redacted>`. Now a denylist of what is actually a credential --
`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-hub-signature-256` and their kin -- and
everything else is data about our own service. The security argument for the
allowlist was "redact everything in case we are compromised", which leaves
nobody able to answer *what did they send* -- the one question that matters
afterwards. Forensics is the thing logs are for; the allowlist removed the
evidence to protect it.

`_path()` stops stripping the query. On a 404 the query is most of what the
caller was trying to do.

## What a refusal now records

The body, capped at 2KB and only when the request was refused (`code >= 400`).
An accepted webhook payload is tens of KB and already in the store, so a copy
per delivery is cost without an answer -- but a refusal has nothing else, and
"what was that caller asking for" is the whole question, whether it is GitHub
pointed at the wrong path or somebody probing.

## What an accepted delivery now records

`webhooks.about()` reads four keys out of the verified payload -- repository,
action, number, target branch -- and puts them on the record. Reading them for
a log line is not the cloud filtering on them: #59 puts routing downstream,
and it stays there; this is answering "what arrived" without opening
Firestore. Never the prose -- a title or a body is someone's words, and
docs/structured-logging.md already puts message content at TRACE and nowhere
else.

Six mutants: the allowlist restored, a refusal recording no body, every
request copying its payload, the query stripped again, `authorization` made
loggable, and the payload fields silently dropped.
